```{r}
# Packages used (call-by-package:: style per the assignment requirement)
library(httr2)
library(jsonlite)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Why an API call instead of rvest::read_html():
# The roster page (https://miamiredhawks.com/sports/swimming-and-diving/roster)
# is a client-side rendered app -- the raw HTML never contains player data,
# so no CSS selector could ever find it. Instead, the page itself calls
# Miami Athletics' public JSON API to fetch the roster. We call that same
# API directly. sportId = 13 is the combined "Swimming and Diving" roster
# (men + women share one roster, distinguished by a "gender" field).
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

rvest::read_html("https://miamiredhawks.com/sports/swimming-and-diving/roster") |> 
  rvest::html_elements("div > a > h3") |>  rvest::html_text2()

resp <- httr2::request("https://miamiredhawks.com/api/v2/Rosters?sportId=13") |>
  httr2::req_perform()
```


```{r}
parsed <- jsonlite::fromJSON(
  httr2::resp_body_string(resp),
  simplifyDataFrame = FALSE
)

players <- parsed$items[[1]]$players

# One row per athlete: full name + class year
build_row <- function(p) {
  data.frame(
    name = trimws(paste(p$firstName, p$lastName)),
    gender = ifelse(is.null(p$gender), NA_character_, p$gender),
    year = ifelse(
      is.null(p$academicYearLong) || p$academicYearLong == "",
      NA_character_,
      p$academicYearLong
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

swim_all <- do.call(rbind, lapply(players, build_row))

# Keep only female and male athletes (drops anything without M/F gender,
# e.g., if a coach or staff record were ever present)
swim_df <- swim_all[swim_all$gender %in% c("M", "F"), c("name", "year")]
rownames(swim_df) <- NULL

swim_df
```
